class_selection_policy.statement: For an issuer with multiple exchange-listed common share classes attached to one earnings event, select a single class deterministically rather than ad hoc: (1) if exactly one listed class is titled plainly 'Common stock' with no series/letter qualifier while other listed classes carry a qualifier, use the plainly-titled class; (2) otherwise, use the class with materially larger public float/shares outstanding, evidenced by a primary or reliable secondary source; (3) if neither rule resolves it (no plain title and float is not materially different), leave the candidate quarantined pending explicit protocol guidance rather than forcing a pick.

foreign_ordinary_shares_policy.statement: A foreign-incorporated issuer's ordinary/common shares that list directly on NASDAQ, NYSE or NYSE American (i.e. the exchange listing itself, not a depositary receipt representing shares held in trust) are treated as in-scope common shares under this pilot's plain-language universe definition ('U.S.-listed common shares'), since they are the issuer's actual common equity and trade identically to domestic common stock on the same market. This policy does not extend to ADRs, which represent a distinct security with potentially different reaction dynamics (currency, arbitrage, liquidity); ADR-structured candidates require separate review.
